text:
Leon Draisaitl is doing the thing he always does when you start to forget about him: scoring in bunches. He has 18 goals in 20 games, eight in his last ten, and a seven-game point streak that includes back-to-back two-goal nights against Vancouver and the Rangers. Even the Rangers' captain, in one headline, was reduced to calling the Oilers' goals "fluky."

Some of them are. Draisaitl has 18 goals on 11.8 expected, shooting 23% against 19% last season, and Edmonton has scored 18.2 more goals than expected with him on the ice. Our talent range sees his finishing settling closer to 17%. Even then, 78 shots in 20 games is the kind of volume that keeps a scorer scoring.

What makes him more than a shooter is the passing. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had him at 14.5 primary shot assists per 60 last season, 99th percentile among forwards, and the Oilers control 61% of five-on-five expected goals when he plays. When the shooting cools, watch whether the assists pick up the slack. In past seasons, they usually have.
headline: Draisaitl is finishing everything, again
